purpose: Customer profiles for analysis/business_metrics.py (plan v2 Part C1). The hour value is the cited BLS figure of results/impact_profile_20261014.json (register row impact-hour-value); the hour-value range below is derived from the same BLS page's percentiles. Every field under a profile's assumptions, and every value in sensitivity, is an ASSUMPTION (a modelling choice, not a measurement) and is labelled so wherever it is used.

hour_value.median_source: results/impact_profile_20261014.json hour_value (register row impact-hour-value): USD 64.44/h, BLS OOH Quick Facts 2025 Median Pay for Software Developers, Quality Assurance Analysts, and Testers

range.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook
range.fetch_method: WebFetch (page converted to text and read back); figures transcribed from that text
quoted: The median annual wage for software developers was $135,980 in May 2025.
The lowest 10 percent earned less than $82,460, and the highest 10 percent earned more than $214,670.
Quick Facts, 2025 Median Pay: "$134,040 per year" and "$64.44 per hour"
range.hours_per_year_derivation: the page gives percentiles as annual wages only (no hourly percentiles). The hourly figures are DERIVED: annual / (group median annual / group median hourly), i.e. the hours per year implied by the page's own Quick Facts pair (134040 / 64.44 = 2080.1).
range.caveat: the percentiles are for software developers alone; the median hour value is the wider group's. Wages, not loaded labour cost; no overhead multiplier.

Supported in part by the laptop's own silent truncation at its default window (blade-k1-layer-split) and its equal decode rate at 4096 (blade-dryrun-rates). The co-runner slowdown (P5) is not transferred: it prints not measured on this laptop.
